answer: A farm faking 277 aliases needs 277 separate permission histories, each built over years, so the cost multiplies per alias instead of staying flat. Planning permission history with council archive is the check: permissions granted and built out over years at one site. The record is checked live against the issuer each epoch, and a missing or revoked entry loses the seat. The knoll record shows the asymmetry: scale multiplies the cost but never the reward, the ferrous entry is checkable by anyone, and the pulse window closes before a farm can catch up.
